title: R1 remote communication contract
description: Protocol package 0.6.1; Worker/Server wire revision 1. D40/D41 preserve current execution identity and TaskStatus. No model credentials, model invocation, attachments, native history, notification channels or signed approvals.

RemoteError.description: Sanitized error. No credential, raw environment, owner locator or arbitrary detail object.

RemoteAccountView.description: Current authenticated account only. No ownerId/accountId selector is exposed.

password.description: Hub Server account password, never a model credential. Never reflected in responses/logs.

csrfToken.description: Session-bound CSRF value, not authentication. Browser authentication remains an HttpOnly Secure cookie.

RemotePairingRequestInput.description: Worker sends its locally generated 256-bit device secret only in Authorization header. Body contains no credential. Unclaimed requests are short-lived authentication challenges, not owner-visible devices.

RemotePairingChallenge.description: Five-minute one-use code; no device secret. Never put the code in a URL.

RemotePairingPreview.description: Authenticated browser preview for explicit device confirmation; does not claim or grant access.

RemotePairingStatusView.description: Device-authenticated status poll scoped to this exact request/credential. Reveals no owner or raw credential.

nextCursor.description: Opaque owner/resource-scoped server cursor; never a Worker seq or cross-owner resource selector.

RemoteDeviceRevocationView.description: Revokes transport rights, does not claim execution was cancelled or stopped.

RemoteEventPosition.description: Highest durably committed contiguous event seq for this Worker store, never the largest observed seq.

wireRevision.description: Worker/Server wire revision, independent of protocol package version. Revision 1 shape is frozen.

protocolVersion.description: Protocol package semantic version for diagnostics only. Never negotiate or reject based on this value.

RemoteWorkerHello.description: First frame after device-authenticated WSS. Same store preserves seq across boots; new store requires null ack. Credentials never appear in frames.

RemoteWorkerHelloAck.description: Frozen delivery requires a reason. Store changes or ack regression require reconciliation; R1 exposes no automatic force-unfreeze API.

supportedWireRevisions.description: Server supported wire revisions, mandatory on rejection (including REMOTE_PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED). Initially [1]; during upgrades advertise N and N-1.

RemoteWorkerHeartbeat.description: Sent every 15 seconds. It reports liveness only, not durable business-event progress.

RemoteServerHeartbeat.description: Heartbeat acknowledgement is not event ack. After 45 seconds without authenticated Worker traffic mark offline without modifying execution state.

RemoteEventAck.description: Only advances after event persistence AND projection/browser-outbox commit; old store ack never trims new store outbox.

RemoteConversationGap.description: Worker requests missing commands or skip records. Never run a later user message across a sequence gap.

parentExecutionTaskId.description: Existing kernel Task.parentTaskId only. Never invented retryOfRunId or a long-lived Task identity.

RemoteResultRef.description: D40: runId is LocalRun, the user-visible control handle. executionTaskId is the current per-run kernel Task; not a long-lived business Task. No Attempt identity.

RemoteControlConfirmed.description: D41: Worker-only structured evidence, never parsed error text. Empty orphanProcessIds is not proof of no remaining process. A paused process may still exist.

executionMayStillBeRunning.description: Must be true for adapter_refused without positive stop evidence. Policy rejection before execution may be false; never infer from terminal label or empty orphan list alone.

RemoteControlRejected.description: D41: Worker-only structured evidence, never parsed error text. Empty orphanProcessIds is not proof of no remaining process. A paused process may still exist.

RemoteControlUnconfirmed.description: D41: Worker-only structured evidence, never parsed error text. Empty orphanProcessIds is not proof of no remaining process. A paused process may still exist.

RemoteRunSubmitPayload.description: References registered Worker workspace and scene revision. No model account/config credentials, arbitrary executable, attachment or server filesystem path. An append message is another run.submit, not mutation of a running turn.

RemoteRunControlPayload.description: All controls address LocalRun. Optional nodeId is valid only for retry of an existing node within this run.

RemoteApprovalDecisionPayload.description: Worker looks up current pending approval/action/policy locally. Browser and server cannot supply a lower risk/action classification.

targetConversationSeq.description: Existing target submit sequence, not a new control sequence. Required to persist an ordered tombstone when withdrawal arrives before the original submit.

RemoteCommandWithdrawalPayload.description: Targets an in-flight submit command whose delivery/acceptance is uncertain. Worker persists a tombstone or stops its bound run; server must not claim success first.

RemoteConversationSkip.description: Durable ordered tombstone for a never-dispatched submit. Not an execution/control command; cannot be used to erase accepted work. Retain until gap replay/snapshot acknowledgement is safe.

RemoteSkipRecorded.description: Worker records ordered skip in the same durable inbox ordering ledger as submits.

RemoteCommandAccepted.description: Durable inbox admission, not model/execution success. Duplicate immutable commands return the original receipt/event.

RemoteCommandRejected.description: Pre-admission rejection only. An expired sequenced submit consumes its ordered slot without execution.

RemoteCommandCompleted.description: Not universally task success. Retry completes on durable new execution reference; execute completes on actual terminal Run success/cancellation. Cancel/pause/resume require confirmed structured control result.

RemoteCommandFailed.description: Failure after admission. A refused control is distinct from unconfirmed cancellation; do not infer that an Agent process has stopped.

RemoteControlObserved.description: D41: unconfirmed leaves command accepted and pending reconciliation. Run-scoped controls include resultRef/executionStatus. Before a Run exists (withdrawal reconciliation), omit both rather than invent an identity or execution state.

parentExecutionTaskId.description: Existing kernel Task.parentTaskId only. Never invented retryOfRunId or a long-lived Task identity.

RemoteRunView.description: Worker-owned execution projection. Offline does not change status. D40 maps LocalRun.taskId to executionTaskId only at remote boundary; existing LocalRunView is unchanged.

RemoteRunStateEvent.description: Worker creates/binds LocalRun and execution Task using existing semantics; it does not invent long-lived Task or retryOfRunId.

text.description: Complete assembled content, never truncated. Resource quota failures are explicit; no partial message is published.

RemoteWorkerMessagePayload.description: Worker may emit assistant/system messages, never impersonate a user or allocate conversationSeq.

RemoteApprovalView.description: Local Worker policy is authoritative. Mandatory blocked actions are git_push/deploy/delete/db_migrate plus locally declared actions; refusal reason code REMOTE_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN. Rejection of a dangerous action may still be submitted remotely.

RemoteProgressEvent.description: Sanitized observable progress only. Never private model reasoning, raw provider auth, full environment, or credential files.

RemoteWorkspaceSummary.description: Worker-exported registered workspace index. displayPath is display-only; no server filesystem path resolution or remote arbitrary folder execution.

RemoteSceneSummary.description: Worker scene index only; model/provider credential or installation/subscription data is not relayed.

RemoteCatalogView.description: Atomic bounded complete catalog for R1. Reject oversized catalogs instead of truncating; offline entries are last observed, not proof that paths still exist.

RemoteConversationView.description: Worker is the sole writer. authority is legacy metadata, never a write gate. Omitted visibility=both, busy=false, busyFresh=false; targetWorkerId is the legacy workerId alias.

RemoteCreateConversationInput.description: Owner/device/workspace/scene references for a Worker-owned creation command. Requires online revision 2; 202 is a transport receipt, not a server-created conversation.

RemoteSendMessageInput.description: Computer orders messages. Offline rejects immediately; revision 2 requires a 30-second delivery grant. Legacy expiresAt cannot extend delivery deadline.

RemoteRunControlInput.description: Path runId is mandatory user-visible identity; only retry may supply nodeId. Does not allocate conversationSeq.

RemoteApprovalDecisionInput.description: Only current owner. approve on blocked action is forbidden in R1; reject does not grant execution permission.

RemoteQueuedReceipt.description: HTTP202 after command and server outbox commit. conversationSeq present only for run.submit. No fabricated runId before Worker assigns it.

RemoteCommandView.description: Three layers must be displayed separately: transport/delivery, Worker controlResult, execution status from RemoteRunView. No inference from disconnected transport or command.completed to task success.

RemoteConversationSnapshot.description: Consistent selected-conversation projection and cursor transaction. For larger history, fetch bounded resource pages while replaying events after this cursor. No whole-history batch or credential content.

RemoteOmittedEvents.description: Worker local event seq continuity without publishing local-only history. Covers inclusive [firstSeq,seq], firstSeq<=seq. Opaque tombstone only, no local conversation/path/model data. Cannot cover any already published event or remote-critical event; immutable bounded ranges are replayed whole. Persist range coverage before advancing contiguous ack.
